name: Crater Lake
note: Crater Lake, Oregon: the caldera of Mount Mazama and the lake in it, from OpenStreetMap on its real ground
attribution: Crater Lake: map data (c) OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL. Elevation: AWS Terrain Tiles. Built by tools/build-osm-city.py.

fetch._: the whole park round the caldera is a detail zone: Rim Village, Mazama Village and the park headquarters are small. extraLand: the forest, the meadows, the rim's cliffs and screes and peaks; extraRoads: the trails, Cleetwood Cove's, the Watchman's, Garfield Peak's, Mount Scott's, Wizard Island's

lakeBed._: the tiles carry the lake as its surface: the bed is cut steeply, as the caldera's walls go on down under the water (594 m at the deepest; the cut stops at 120 m, which no view sees past)

terrain._: the lake at 1883 m (the datum), the rim from 2100 to 2480 m at Hillman Peak and 2721 m at Mount Scott: elevation from tools/fetch-terrain.py

_lakeColour: the blue of very deep, very clean water: the lake absorbs every other colour of the sunlight and scatters the blue back

defaultHeights._: the park's buildings are low and steep-roofed against the snow; the lodge is modelled (src/crater/landmarks.js)

pitchAll._: every roof pitched, steep, for the snow

lake.name: Crater Lake

landmarks.name: Crater Lake Lodge
landmarks.info: Opened in 1915 on the rim, 300 m over the water: stone below, bark shingle above, a roof full of dormers. By the 1980s it was near collapse under the winters' snow; it was taken apart and rebuilt, keeping its look, and reopened in 1995. Its lake terrace is where people come to sit in the evening.

landmarks.name: Sinnott Memorial Overlook
landmarks.info: A stone overlook built into the caldera wall under Rim Village in 1931, with the best of the views 270 m over the water; inside, the story of how the lake was made.

landmarks.name: The Watchman Lookout
landmarks.info: A fire lookout of 1932 on the Watchman, 2,442 m, on the west rim over Wizard Island: a stone ground floor and the glazed cab on it. A trail of 1.3 km climbs to it from the Rim Drive.

landmarks.name: Mount Scott Lookout
landmarks.info: Mount Scott, 2,721 m, the highest point in the park: a parasitic cone on Mazama's east flank, older than the collapse. The lookout on its summit is still staffed in the fire season.

landmarks.name: The Phantom Ship
landmarks.info: A spine of andesite some 400,000 years old, the oldest rock exposed in the caldera, standing out of the water off the south shore: 50 m high and 150 m long, its spires like a ship's masts, and from the rim at dusk or in mist it seems to come and go.

landmarks.name: Wizard Island
landmarks.info: A cinder cone 230 m high that grew out of the caldera's floor after the collapse, with a crater 30 m deep at its top. The tour boats land here; a trail climbs to the summit.

landmarks.name: Llao Rock
landmarks.info: A cliff 600 m over the water on the north rim: the cross-section of a lava flow that filled a valley on Mazama's flank shortly before the climactic eruption. It is named for Llao, the spirit of the world below in the Klamath account of the mountain's fall.

landmarks.name: Cleetwood Cove
landmarks.info: The only place the public can reach the water: a trail of 1.8 km down 210 m of switchbacks to the dock. The boat tours leave from here; people swim, and jump from the rock beside the dock into water that is 13 °C in summer.

landmarks.name: Mount Mazama
landmarks.info: The volcano that stood here, some 3,700 m high, until about 7,700 years ago: its eruption emptied the chamber beneath it and its summit fell in. The lake fills the hole.

landmarks.name: Pumice Castle
landmarks.info: An outcrop of orange pumice in the east wall, eroded into towers and battlements.

landmarks.name: Hillman Peak
landmarks.info: The highest point on the rim, 2,488 m, cut in half by the collapse: a cone's cross-section in the wall.

landmarks.name: Devils Backbone
landmarks.info: A dike, a wall of lava that welled up through a crack in the old mountain and set, now standing out of the caldera wall from rim to water.

landmarks.name: Discovery Point
landmarks.info: Where John Wesley Hillman, prospecting for gold, is said to have first seen the lake, in 1853.

landmarks.name: Rim Village
landmarks.info: The lodge, the café and the visitor centre on the south rim, where most people first see the lake.

landmarks.name: Sun Notch
landmarks.info: A U-shaped notch in the south rim, cut by a glacier on the old mountain, over the Phantom Ship.

_dropAreas: the forest and the park's boundary are mapped as great polygons; src/crater/ground.js paints the ground and plants the trees itself
